findings.title: Specify how an existing durable Workflow obtains a genuine committed Sources frame after owner restart
findings.evidence: The only specified Sources wiring is prepare before initialize for a first drive. New ManagedWorkflowSources starts with no TaskSources; prepare refuses whenever a Workflow record already exists; both capture and committed_input require a pre-existing in-memory frame before they inspect any retained artifact. Workflow retry only clears the exact old reservation and then the next step calls these inputs again. Section8 classifies existing published artifacts and promises fresh retry/resumption but does not define a new retained-frame installation or pre-artifact restart preparation port/transaction. Current-epoch ResultStore.verify alone does not install a Sources frame. The inherited agent-execution design requires later source ports to consume retained objects and expressly forbids reconstructing old PreparedExecutor provenance, so neither reusing prepare nor calling initialize again provides this missing contract.
findings.causal_trigger: Restart after a genuine successful Implement publication while the nonterminal Workflow still has later phases. The new owner correctly fences old grants and verifies the durable artifact, but the fresh Sources map is empty. The next step fails committed-input preparation; calling prepare fails existing-Workflow rejection. The analogous crash after Workflow initialization and before first native adoption has no artifact and needs a genuine fresh preparation/Workflow recovery transition. These are explicitly required RS-R3/RS-AC7 recovery stages, not an absent optional gate.
findings.impact: Safe recoverable Tasks cannot reach the advertised resumed or explicitly fresh retry path with the proposed consumer wiring. An implementer must invent the missing authority boundary, and a naive workaround risks reconstructing the old live capability or replacing Workflow/history/Context authority. Unsupported holds are safe but do not fulfill the specified supported restart/recovery control.
findings.requested_change: Define distinct private typed recovery routes for an existing Workflow: verified current-epoch retained-artifact source-frame installation with exact artifact/dependencies/current accepted governing policy/Task/Workflow/generation/Context CAS, and a pre-artifact fresh preparation recovery route that journals a new unit/namespace before effects and atomically records the explicit recovery disposition/history. Name the actual Sources and Workflow consumers, cancellation/abandonment behavior, and classify unsupported cases visibly. Do not fabricate initial adoption capability or overwrite initialize/history. Preserve existing revoked grants and prerequisite artifact pins.

findings.title: Per-member quota admission and unconditional serialization omit the required frozen channel/cohort admission contract
evidence: The proposed requirements explicitly preserve every Issue9 independent-input obligation except the named custody/death, live-worktree lock and cleanup-dependent release overrides (requirements lines20-29).

Pinned Issue9 I9-AC-8.k (lines2220-2248) requires qualification of the actual frozen roster/source-key/timing/permit schedule, queued-member elapsed-envelope checks, and COMPLETE global/Project/provider permit acquisition all-or-nothing for concurrent-only cohorts; a waiting cohort holds zero partial permits.

The design instead says Runtime permits may serialize members (lines77-78), reserves each queued worker independently (139-142), and directs every member to the existing NativeSessions/QuotaScheduler lease admission (186-189). No whole-cohort reservation, finite qualified admission envelope, queued-member timing revalidation, or distinction between serialized-capable and concurrent-only qualification appears in either new document.

At the actual baseline, NativeSessions::start_inner calls QuotaScheduler::admission for one Unit (execution/native.rs312-329). Store::reserve_execution_quota_with_project_limit checks and inserts a single Unit lease in its transaction (state/execution/quotas.rs149-234,302-333). Thus the reused primitive does not already supply cohort atomicity.
findings.causal_rationale: A legitimate concurrent-only qualified two-member profile can start its first member after one per-Unit lease while its second member waits for capacity; or two competing cohorts can each retain one member permit. Serializing the rest or admitting outside the proven start window invalidates the profile evidence for current-peer input independence. The proposed aggregate compares current hashes and counts but has no durable qualified-schedule predicate to prevent certifying that round. This is independent of physical cleanup/death proof and is not superseded by the new result-protection profile.
findings.minimal_correction: Freeze the exact registered channel qualification and permitted schedule with the roster. Add a real cohort-level atomic global/Project/provider lease reservation for concurrent-only profiles (zero partial leases while waiting); constrain serialized admission to a proven serialized-capable envelope and recheck elapsed schedule/qualification at every member pre-input grant. Reject or make the entire round noncertifying on startup/envelope mismatch while preserving existing owners/results. Do not silently serialize a concurrent-only profile or qualify independence by provider-family labels.
proposed_causal_controls_not_executed: Two two-member concurrent-only cohorts compete for capacity three: exactly one acquires two leases; the other has zero leases and zero native input, then progresses after the first logically closes under the new profile.

A serialized-capable profile starts member one, then healthy contention delays member two beyond its frozen qualification window: member-two input zero and certificate zero; member-one historical outcome remains retained.
Compile omissions of all-or-nothing cohort admission and queued pre-input schedule validation; restored real consumers must pass and each omission must fail its intended assertion.
